analysis: Examined the docs/provider/troubleshooting.md base and head text and the ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift patch. The Swift change is a one-line addition at head line ~207: when an add-on hold begins (TB-012, T-059), `selectedModelRecovery.attempt?.task.cancel()` now also cancels any in-flight selected-model recovery load, alongside the existing preloadTasks cancellation. This tightens the hold's model-load fence, so a recovery attempt does not load a model beside the add-on's VMs. It adds no attack surface, no new authorization path and no data exposure. I did not see how settleAddonHold or the recovery scheduler handle a cancelled attempt. They could possibly restart a recovery attempt during an active hold, or leave cancelled-state bookkeeping inconsistent. That would be a residual availability or fence-completeness question for T-059/A-018, not a demonstrated regression. The task is cancelled via optional chaining, and the visible patch shows no new privilege. The docs change adds troubleshooting rows for drain failures (head line 135) and selected-model recovery (head lines 169-171). These describe operator-run commands and the existing load-gate behavior. They introduce no new security claim or trust-policy change. The `--force` advice is limited to interrupting unfinished work. Selected-model recovery is described as evicting only idle models outside the selection, with no Autopilot hold, pin or lease, which is consistent with the existing hold semantics. Remaining integration question: confirm that the recovery scheduler respects the add-on hold (does not re-arm while the serving drain owner is .addonHold) and that load admission itself also checks the hold. This is outside the supplied evidence.
